evidence: The workbook Quality Checks D21 and Internal Quality Checks D21 both require a 'committed, static baseline'; quality-checks.md:88 repeats this. The frozen source is static and deterministic on pinned values, but exact R2 reference bytes are not committed. Independent git status and git show HEAD:<path> comparisons in per-row-review/evidence/20/source-binding.json (SHA256 dc59585a5c0b63fc5d285e886e08934fda1da0b8acd9af7c175b0af569792557) show three tracked reference files modified (public/index.html, public/js/app.js, src/index.js) and two untracked modules (public/js/change-sets.js, src/change-sets.js) under projects/hireops-recruiting-operations/hireops-recruiting-operations/solution. Every working source file matches frozen task bytes, so this is about the reviewed reference, not another checkout. No exact-byte committed R2 archive is known; the current ZIP is also uncommitted. The current ZIP does independently match all frozen task files and has SHA256 8bf362f1f18defa08c1ce60f6ba1e79cb8423993134eb17186b7f20aea34f440. Deterministic substance is sound: solve.sh:33 copies the supplied app; db.js:122-179 seeds fixed local JSON IDs/values transactionally and does not reseed existing users; db.js:132-133 stores reference_moment; rules.js:17-21 reads that stored clock and :142-150 computes referral vesting from it; index.js:49 sends timestamps through that clock. The bundled and public seed match SHA256 1b39015461a7a4f23b835aeea9584caffd0266c64d394778376cbd6c8a18bcf7. Random session tokens (index.js:99), change-set IDs (change-sets.js:87) and collision-fallback successor IDs are unpinned identities, explicitly allowed by public rules:203-204 and not seed randomness. No fetched seed, regenerated source or wall-clock-based graded amount was found. Verified indexed lifecycle driver/log/results hashes (05780ac5eb6f1e441ef5a946a36f466ad7cdee7ae239b5f7d7d9f5933f39e024 / 8b69cb9273df6a299154a83f8cc42b166216bbc856c51233bc95cd45859287f9 / 52b5ba96bded2e133fe4ec16117c150d46673f70ce31284169193f478c73e9f9), all 13 recorded solution-app hashes against frozen source, and current manifest/artifact-binding hashes. Lifecycle observations include fresh installation, retained data through actual MCP process replacement, and clean reinstall returning 7 requisitions/13 offers; those finite observations do not claim full configured grading or identical whole-database bytes.
counterexample: Reproducing the candidate from the recorded Git HEAD omits both change-sets.js modules and retains earlier index/UI bytes, so a checkout cannot reconstruct the coordinated-change baseline that this frozen review and ZIP test. A reviewer accepting only the existence of a static working tree could pass this unreproducible committed baseline. A separate temporal broken-app probe would replace R.refAt(db) with the OS clock: seeded OFF-110 referral (start 2026-02-10) would incorrectly vest $10,000 on 2026-10-01 instead of $5,000 at fixed 2026-08-01; inspected reference code avoids it. Conforming alternative considered: cryptographically random session tokens or generated change-set IDs with stable stored associations are permitted and must not falsely fail merely because those unpinned strings differ across installations.
suggested_fix: Commit the exact reviewed reference bytes (or an exact-byte reproducible source snapshot) and verify the committed tree against the frozen solution hashes; preserve current deterministic seed/clock behavior and existing evidence.
